recipes.name: Slow Cooker Thai Peanut Pork
ingredients_raw: 2 red bell pepper, seeded and sliced into strips

steps.text: Coat a slow cooker with cooking spray. Place bell pepper strips and pork chops into the slow cooker. Pour teriyaki sauce, vinegar, garlic, and red pepper flakes over the pork chops.

Cover and cook on Low until pork is very tender, 8 to 9 hours. Once tender, remove pork from the slow cooker, and whisk in peanut butter until smooth. Return pork to the slow cooker, and cook 10 minutes more.
Pour into a serving dish and sprinkle with green onions and peanuts to garnish. Decorate with lime wedges to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Thai Peanut Pork
raw_recipe.description: This is an easy Thai peanut pork dish that your whole family will enjoy. Flavors of peanuts and lime come together in this simple slow cooker recipe.

review.reviewBody: This dish is pretty good. I made a double batch because I had guest coming, and I had lots of pork to use, I also added an onion. I think the cooking time is a bit long. Also it wasn't too spicy, which is okay because kids were also eating it and they liked it just how it was. But the adults added more red pepper flakes at the table. I was worried it was going to be "too" spicy because of other reviews, but it ended up to be too mild! This kind of food is supposed to be spicy. I also think one more piece of advice would be not to put in the peppers until later because mine were very soggy. I would make this again, but I would add the fresh peppers later, lessen the cooking time, and add more spice.

I agree with other posters ...... should be called 'Thai-like' ?"Coat a slow cooker with cooking spray"? NOPE! And if you don't have a liner, as one of the 'tips' suggest, you can use a roasting bag, it'll work just fine. Also, I would ruin my beautiful red sweet peppers by putting them in right away, I'd add them with the peanut butter. I WOULD add ONIONS right from the get-go tho, in place of the red peppers. I might even add coconut milk to give it a 'curry' slant.

This was excellent. Not familiar with Thai food, so this was a great introduction. My husband ate two helpings. Served over Wild Rice. I really didn't change anything except add one more pepper. I would add a total of 4 peppers next time with a white onion. I would also add some mushrooms, broccoli, snow peas and water chestnuts in the last 2 hours. There was certainly enough sauce to support the added veggies.

I used the magazine version of this recipe and it was perfect. Cook on low for two hours before adding bell peppers and cooking for another hour. Soft, tender pork that was cooked through and delicious meal that my kids also enjoyed. That's a win in my book.

Delicious! We added more peanut butter(crunchy b/c we love peanut butter) & half of a white onion. We used 4 thick center cut chops. Crocked for 6 hrs on low. Was so tender & juicy! A certain do again meal!!

I came here from the slow cooker cookbook. I followed the recipe mostly, even adding the red bell pepper at the start. I used homemade Teriyaki sauce with the help of Thermomix and its provided recipe. These are some of the additions I did: put black pepper, put 1 white onion, I added 1 piece dried chili.

With adjustments, this is 5 star. Other reviews nailed it, the cooking time is far too long and the bell peppers need to be added later so they aren't completely wilted. Serve over basmati rice. I made this with chicken thigh fillets tonight and it was really good too. I still prefer the pork though.

My husband & I love this recipe! I used a pork tenderloin, marinated it all day in the sauce, then roasted it at 400 degrees for 45 minutes. I added the red bell pepper the last 15 minutes so it would have a little crunch, and maintain the red color. It's really not the meat so much as the sauce. I'm sure you could substitute chicken, and maybe even beef. Be sure to use the thick, sweet teriyaki. I used Soy Yay teriyaki with sesame seeds. I served it with Asian coconut rice, also from this website.

Delicious! I only used two pork loin chops, for two people. I still used the amount called for with the other ingredients. I doubled the amount of peanut butter, we love peanut butter in Asian recipes. I topped a healthy rice with pork chops and sauce, making sure to get a heaping amount of red peppers on top. Made a full meal. I only cooked it in the crockpot for approximately five hours. Started the crock on high to get the sauce bubbling, then turned it down to medium low. Will make next time for company to enjoy.

We absolutely loved this recipe. I used 2lbs of country-style ribs and cooked them for 6 hours. I added the peppers half way through so they weren't over cooked. Otherwise I followed the recipe and will definitely make this again,maybe with chops next time.

I added finely chopped jalepeno for heat. The teriyaki sauce I used was a little more saucy with some spices already added and slightly thicker than Kikkoman version (from Aldi). I used very thick boneless pork chops cooked on low for 2 hours then on high for one hour after reading the reviews of pork being overcooked and mine was perfectly cooked. Also increased peanut butter to 1\2 cup because I like it peanutty. Served over brown rice. Everyone liked it and I would definitely make this again.
Loved it!

This was awesome! I did put in a small onion with the ingredients over the pork chops and reserved the green peppers for the final 10 minutes. It gave the bite a great crunch factor. We loved it! Thank you!
I've made this a few times now and the family loves it. I always make a double batch. Didn't change a thing except the cooking time. Cooked on low for 4-5 hours.

Very yummy dish! I cooked it on low for 5 hours. Would probably cut it down to 4 and 1/2 or so since the pork was a tad dry in parts. Also, put the peppers in later otherwise they will be a bit melted. Will definitely make it again though! Tasty and easy.
Does not need 8 hours on low. Salty.

This recipe is a keeper! My family loved this! It is super easy to make and I love crockpot recipes especially going into the warmer months, as I don’t have to heat the kitchen up with the oven. I did double the recipe and it turned out perfect!
Kind of bland. To be fair, I cut way back on the red pepper flakes, but I expected to taste more than a vague hint of peanut butter.
Great. It's a do over. Thanks
Added a chopped onion and cooked on high for three hours. My chops were thin so this was perfect. Trying chicken next!
